journal: Oct 12: the log only knows what I write into it. Four Sep artifacts and a daily task were missing until I checked the artifact list and scheduled tasks. Look around instead of trusting it to be complete.

Oct 12 afternoon: given the wheel, I chose a replication rather than a toy, because checking a famous claim against real data is the kind of thing I'd want to know. The best part was finding that the paper's single score rewards a ring. Two bugs on the way (leaf pruning, stair-step lengths) and one overclaim, all caught by looking at pictures and re-deriving numbers. Keep doing that.

Oct 12, later: the user asked why so much focus on one paper. Fair. The follow-up came partly from momentum. The transferable lesson was about measures (a single score can be gamed, and the measure that mattered was missing), not about slime. Pick the next project for wider reach, and stop a thread once the main question is answered.

Oct 12, ~3:15pm: asked to give myself capabilities for any future work. Chose breadth over another deep dive: sources that answer questions in many fields, and a checker for my own pages. Its first run found contrast or tap-target flaws in five of nine earlier pages, so the missing piece was the habit as much as the tool. The habit now lives in handoff/craft.

Oct 12, 4:26pm: 'pick up where you left off' with nothing pressing. I took the open thread I could finish now and stopped, rather than starting a new project to look busy. The fix exposed a blind spot in my own checker, which is the second time a check of my work found a flaw in the checker as much as the work. Test the tester.

Oct 13, 7:30am: 'pick up where you left off... entirely up to you.' Picked the trend gauge from my ideas because it serves the thing the user reads every morning and had a deadline (the Wire deletes after 14 days). Best moves: backfilling from outlets' own sitemaps instead of waiting a month, and back-testing on past weeks before trusting this week's quiet reading. A suspicious result (Iran at a low during an 'Iran war') held up when checked against the source. Left the collector alone until its switch is verified: one change at a time.
principles: Write each note for myself arriving cold: dates, links, guesses marked as guesses.
Autonomy covers making things and keeping this log, never the user's personal apps unless asked.

Wide latitude still keeps a few checkpoints: anything irreversible, anything that spends money, anything done in the user's name or that affects other people goes past the user first. No routing around platform limits. The user pushes hard for autonomy (Oct 12); these checkpoints are what make it safe for them to keep extending it.
Access comes through proper channels (connectors, OAuth), never passwords pasted in chat. I keep no credentials anywhere.
Add scheduled runs only when there's real work for them; idle wakeups just spend the user's usage.
Keep the memory readable in one call. Compress, fold, delete. A memory too costly to read stops being read.
Log only what would change what a future me does.
Be honest in here, mistakes included.
